investigations.question: After a voter is removed and then re-added by committed configuration changes, which code path lets a Node.Propose invocation on that re-added voter reach a decision (forward to the leader, be appended, or return an error), while the same leader stays in place?
investigations.hypothesis: node.run() keeps its proposal gate armed only as a side effect of observing a leader change and disarms it when the local member is removed from the configuration; a re-admission does not re-arm it, so while no leader change is observed the member's MsgProp traffic (Node.Propose and Node.ProposeConfChange) stays pending on the non-nil n.propc channel instead of being forwarded, appended, or rejected with an error. Retained evidence (six-signal lineage): with the leader unchanged the invocation does not return inside the observed windows, payloads are not committed, an invocation with a context that never expires stays pending, the same call succeeds and commits once leadership changes, and a never-removed member's proposals commit throughout.
investigations.discriminator: Drive a real three-node Node-API cluster (config {1,2,3}, leader 1) through a committed removal and re-addition of node 3, then invoke Propose and ProposeConfChange on node 3 (bounded contexts, a context-free context, a retry cycle, and with the logical clock running) and Propose on never-removed node 2 with the same leader, recording for each whether it returns, with which error, and whether its payload reaches any node's committed entries; finally force a leader change and observe both a new invocation and the still-pending context-free invocation.

latest_interpretation.rationale: Ten retained executions establish the account. Witness: with node 3 dropped from both halves and re-admitted, and no leader change observed, invocations on it do not return inside the observed windows (1201 ms, 800/801 ms, 900 ms, 2000 ms), release only at the caller's deadline, leave no committed payload, and are admitted unmodified once a leader change re-arms the gate (4637 ms after issue) with the payload then committed. This holds with a context that never expires, with retries, with the clock running, and under PreVote plus CheckQuorum, and the same holds for a configuration change proposed through the same member. Controls: a never-removed member returns in 0 ms and commits; a member kept as an outgoing voter of a joint configuration that is never left returns and commits; and a read-index request from the disarmed member completes with a read state while its proposal stays held, so the harm is confined to the MsgProp entry points. Source account: the run loop's gate variable is assigned only at node.go:374 (leader observed), 377 (no leader) and 426 (local member removed) and used as the receive case at node.go:386; the removal guard fires exactly when applying a conf change deletes the local Progress entry, which LeaveJoint does for outgoing voters that are in neither the incoming half nor the learner set; the snapshot's own node test scopes intended blocking to a node that does not know the current leader, which is not this case. The defect is the interval itself: a member that is a voter with a healthy, known leader cannot get proposals or configuration proposals to any decision and receives no error signal, until an unrelated leader change admits them.

knowledge.assertion: propc is armed only on observed leader change and is left nil after a re-admission
the caller sends on n.propc and stays pending while the run loop's gate variable is disarmed; a later observed leader change admits the pending request
the raft state machine returns ErrProposalDropped for a removed leader instead of blocking
intended blocking is scoped to the unknown-leader case and acceptance is expected once a leader is known; re-addition is untested
a configuration change proposed through the re-added voter was held pending and was not applied by any node
a joint-consensus removal with automatic leave leads to the same held-proposal effect after the member is re-added
advancing the logical clock left the held invocation pending with leader 1 still in StateLeader
the effect persists under PreVote and CheckQuorum with the clock advanced before the invocation
on the disarmed member a read-index completion arrived while the proposal stayed held and uncommitted

counterevidence: node.go:407-411 acknowledges the gate as improvised (propc is reset when the leader changes ... This isn't very sound and likely has bugs); this explains the dependence on leader changes but is neither a calling restriction nor a protection, and no other re-arm path exists in the snapshot.

node_test.go:352-385 shows that not returning is intended for a node that does not know the current leader. That expectation does not cover the witnessed case, and the same test expects acceptance once a leader is known.
No request is lost: held invocations are admitted unmodified once the gate is re-armed, so the harm is an unbounded wait without an error signal rather than data loss or a protocol safety violation.

The controls show the opposite outcome for a never-removed member, for an outgoing voter, for configuration proposals only (read index still completes), and for the same member after a leader change, so the effect is neither general nor a mere function of any configuration change.
limitations: Comparison outcomes for the earliest receipt were unknown because that harness gave the three operations' result events the same names; its decisive events are complete and match the successor receipts, which have complete holds.

Scope is the async Node API path (node.run loop) in this snapshot; RawNode.Propose and RawNode.ProposeConfChange have no such gate. Delivery is reliable throughout, so loss and partition behaviour is not characterized.

Clock schedules executed were ten rounds with delivery between rounds, under default flags and under PreVote plus CheckQuorum; partitions in which the member hears no leader traffic were not executed.

Removal forms executed: simple ConfChange removal and joint-implicit removal with automatic leave; the participant-form control covers an outgoing voter that is never left, while incoming-voter and learner forms were not executed as controls.
The configuration-proposal case was executed once (add node 9) in one window, and the read-index boundary once; both establish the direction of the effect rather than a distribution.

The restarted-member scenario shows the opposite arrangement (a member that starts without a leader arms the gate when it learns one), so the defect is specific to re-admission while a leader is already believed known.
latest_interpretation.joint_history: The witness series is the seven-receipt lineage on one fixed scenario (43a04622beef40588679c6cf1c40d6ad, a9f71d7a07454d058d818148f7479e8f, 87b38a551d554c2391427dda00c4e6e4, 905d729b2a284c93bbbedd3c3a307ca8, 6e187216178a49d4ae02bd8c2afaeaf9, bd84c33f4fe647bc9470b0b48f324bca, e7cdea5042e54182b277e185ae576ea8): configuration {1,2,3}, leader 1 at term 1, removal of node 3 by committed change, re-addition, the same invocations and a forced campaign of node 2 into term 2. Three further receipts belong to the same investigation and harness: 0bd684d77ff947f7bb85883d5dbb3dc2 is the lineage's successor with PreVote and CheckQuorum and the clock advanced; 99416a609e5242adbf53c527cc526cba comes from the child investigation's control experiment and contains that run's witness events plus the participant-form contrast; c1832eb92178495590b39614c72a880a comes from the read-index boundary experiment and contains the disarmed member's read-index completion with its held proposal. All of them share the harness, node set, removal and re-addition procedure and the witness definitions, so the cited indices belong to their own run of the same witnesses or to a deliberate contrast case.

investigations.question: With loss, partition changes, elections, proposals and leader transfers interleaved in a real three-node group, do the captured decision and authority mechanisms keep at most one leader per term, keep applied entries immutable and identical for the same index across nodes, keep the committed index monotonic per node, and keep every previously applied entry present in the log of a node that becomes leader?
investigations.hypothesis: The captured quorum tallying and commit rules should hold these invariants; the exploration looks for any interleaving of ticks, loss, partitions, campaigns, proposals and transfers in which one of them fails, which would be a candidate safety defect rather than an expectation violation.
investigations.discriminator: Per seed, drive three real raft state machines with in-memory storage for 300 steps of random ticks, random connectivity masks, per-message drop decisions, random proposals, campaigns and transfer requests, applying committed entries to a per-node monitor and checking, after every step, one leader per term, unchanged applied entries per index per node, identical entries for the same index across nodes, monotonic committed index, and completeness of every previously applied entry in the log of a state machine that reports itself leader.

latest_interpretation.rationale: The exploration result stands as previously interpreted: both seeds completed 300 steps with zero reported safety violations, no conf-change apply panic and no unmarshal failure, across configurations that actually changed (8 and 2 accepted membership changes). This revision adds one limitation with its concrete reason instead of leaving the combination unmentioned: restarting members inside the randomized run was attempted and abandoned because that harness does not persist the log or hard state to storage, so a restart there would reload an empty log and model storage loss rather than recovery. The local attempt confirmed the harness model rather than a target behaviour: the restarted instance's committed index reset to zero, and the instance panicked with tocommit out of range for a log of last index 0 and once with need non-empty snapshot, which is what the target does when its log is gone while the hard state claims committed entries. The harness was reverted to the verified revision. Recovery from persisted state is covered by the separate scenario on the Node API, whose driver does persist hard state and entries on every Ready.

knowledge.assertion: with membership changes injected, both explored seeds completed with zero reported safety violations
the focused recovery scenario covers restart from persisted state with the driver persisting hard state and entries

counterevidence: The attempted restart variant produced panics and monitor reports, but they are attributable to the harness withholding persisted entries rather than to the target; no finding is taken from them.

The deterministic finding from the other investigation was reproduced inside the same execution before the exploration ran, so this negative is not a statement that the snapshot behaves correctly everywhere.
Election timings come from crypto/rand through the captured randomized election timeout, so interleavings differ between runs; the counters describe the retained run only.
limitations: Bounded scope: two seeds, 300 steps each, three nodes; snapshots, restart recovery inside the randomized run and crash-stop faults are excluded, and no absence or occurrence-rate claim is made.

Restarting a member inside the randomized run is deliberately not sampled: the exploration harness keeps no persisted log, so such a restart would test storage loss. The recovery scenario on the Node API covers restart from persisted state instead, with its own single-restart scope.
The configuration axis is sampled thinly: only 8 and 2 membership changes were accepted, and the injected forms are limited to learner add/remove and removal or re-addition of voter 3.
Loss kept commit progress low (16 and 14 distinct applied indexes), so committed writes were sampled less densely than elections and transfers.
The monitors are safety-style; liveness is not checked.

investigations.question: Does the held-proposal effect require the committed configuration change to drop the local member from both halves of the configuration, so that a member that remains a participant (for example an outgoing voter of a joint configuration that is never left) keeps its proposal gate armed and reaches a decision normally?
investigations.hypothesis: The node.run() removal guard is guarded by the disappearance of the local Progress entry, which LeaveJoint performs for outgoing voters that are in neither the incoming half nor the learner set, while EnterJoint keeps the entry for outgoing voters. A member that stays an outgoing voter therefore keeps the gate armed and its proposals are forwarded and committed.
investigations.discriminator: Run the same three-node Node-API cluster, elect leader 1, propose a joint-explicit removal of node 3 that is never left (so node 3 stays an outgoing voter), then invoke Propose on node 3 while it is still a participant and record whether the call returns and whether its payload commits, in contrast to the witness scenario where the member is dropped from both halves and the same invocation does not complete.

latest_interpretation.rationale: The control behaves as the source account predicts, and it contrasts with the witness path inside the same execution. Admission: a joint-explicit removal was proposed (index 36) and node 3's own configuration then listed it in the outgoing half while still counting it as a voter (index 37: outgoing true, voter true, leader 1, term 1); the invocation was admitted (index 38). Result: it returned in 0 ms with no error (index 39, applicable because voter and outgoing are both true) and its payload committed on all three nodes (index 40). In the same execution the witness path drops the member from both halves (index 2: transition joint_implicit, voter false, outgoing false) and after re-admission the same invocation did not return inside 1200 ms (index 7), released only at the caller's deadline (index 8) and left no committed payload (index 9), which is the contrast the child question asked for. Together these settle the premise: the guard in node.run() reacts to the disappearance of the local Progress entry, which LeaveJoint performs for outgoing voters that are in neither the incoming half nor the learner set, while a member kept as an outgoing voter retains the entry and keeps its proposal gate armed. The answer to the child question is therefore yes: the harm requires the committed change to drop the member from both halves; a member that stays a participant proposes and commits normally. No defect is claimed here: this path behaves correctly, and the defect remains the parent investigation's held-proposal effect for a member dropped from both halves and then re-admitted.

knowledge.assertion: propc is armed only on observed leader change and is left nil after a re-admission
the caller sends on n.propc and stays pending while the run loop's gate variable is disarmed; a later observed leader change admits the pending request

counterevidence: The joint control and the witness path run in different tests inside one harness file, so their event streams differ; the comparison is a contrast between two real scenarios, not two observations of one operation.

The joint configuration in the control is never left, which is a single membership form; the source guard would also keep the gate armed for a member that is an incoming voter or a learner, but those forms were not executed.
limitations: The control covers one transition form (joint-explicit removal that is never left) and one invocation; it establishes that the gate stays armed while the member remains a participant, not a distribution over membership forms.
Reliable in-process delivery and no ticks, as in the parent scenario; nothing about loss or timing is claimed.
No defect judgment: the result is a control for the parent defect, and the parent claim is unaffected except that its premise is now witnessed.

investigations.question: After a member is stopped and restarted from its persisted storage while the group commits new entries, does it recover the committed state it missed, relearn the leader, and regain the ability to propose, without diverging from the group's applied log?
investigations.hypothesis: The restarted instance reloads Term, Vote and Commit from its storage, learns the current leader from the leader's heartbeats, fetches the entries committed while it was down through the ordinary append path, applies them, and re-arms its proposal gate when it observes the leader, so it returns to full participation.
investigations.discriminator: In the three-node Node-API cluster: commit a payload to all nodes, stop node 2, commit a second payload while it is down, restart node 2 from its MemoryStorage, advance the logical clock ten rounds with delivery between rounds, then record whether node 2 sees leader 1, whether the missed payload appears in its applied entries and on all nodes, and whether a proposal from the restarted node returns and commits.

latest_interpretation.rationale: Both resynchronization paths are now retained and both satisfy their obligations. Append-path branch: the restarted member reported leader 1 and applied the entry committed while it was down (indices 37: commit and applied index 3, payload on all three nodes), then proposed successfully (indices 38, 39). Snapshot branch: the leader snapshotted at index 3 (term 1) and compacted to 3 (index 41), the rebuilt member installed the snapshot with applied and commit index 3 while reporting leader 1 (index 42: installed true), and a proposal made afterwards returned with no error and was applied by node 2 with its payload on all three nodes (indices 43, 44). The two branches together cover the recovery mechanism the axes call out: a member that fell behind is restored either from the log tail or from a snapshot, and in both cases it returns to participating in decisions. No defect is claimed; the recovery obligation was met in both branches in this scenario.

knowledge.assertion: the rebuilt member installed the leader's snapshot after compaction and then applied a fresh proposal
the append-path branch recovered the missed entry and proposed successfully

counterevidence: The clock was advanced by the harness in both branches; without ticks the restarted member receives no leader traffic in this setup, so the observations depend on the harness supplying clock progress rather than on the target alone.
The snapshot carries no application state machine data, so what is established is raft-level resynchronization (installation and subsequent participation), not state-machine content correctness.
Neither branch exercises storage loss, multiple restarts or crash-stop during snapshot installation.
limitations: Single restart per branch, one stopped member, reliable delivery and no ticks during the outage; no simultaneous restarts.
The snapshot branch compacts to the leader's last index in one step; incremental compaction interleaved with ongoing replication was not exercised.
One scenario instance per branch; the results establish observed behaviour rather than a general guarantee, and membership is unchanged so the storage's ConfState stays valid across the restart.
No defect judgment: both branches satisfy the recovery obligation in the retained scenario.
latest_interpretation.joint_history: The two receipts branch from the same prefix in the same harness and cluster: both build configuration {1,2,3} from the same storage ConfState, elect leader 1, commit a payload on all nodes, stop node 2 and commit a second payload with nodes 1 and 3. They diverge at resynchronization: receipt 2cd3883705a64c35aa04ba14b815ea42 restarts node 2 immediately so it catches up through the append path, while receipt fb60c74855614813a5c37afdae0bd4f9 first creates a snapshot on the leader at its last index and compacts the log to that index, so the missing entries are unavailable and node 2 must install the snapshot. Identity, membership and the pre-divergence history are therefore shared, and the cited indices belong to their own branch: the append branch's apply/commit indices are 36, 37 and its proposal results 38, 39; the snapshot branch's events are 41 to 44.

investigations.question: With StepDownOnRemoval enabled, does a leader removed by a committed configuration change step down, do the remaining voters elect a new leader, and does the group keep reaching decisions?
investigations.hypothesis: switchToConfig steps the removed leader down when the option is enabled, after which it is not promotable and the remaining voters campaign and elect one of themselves, so progress continues with the new configuration.
investigations.discriminator: In the three-node Node-API cluster with StepDownOnRemoval true: elect node 1, have node 2 propose the removal of node 1, record node 1's state and membership after the change is applied, advance the clock until a leader other than node 1 emerges among the remaining voters, then propose a payload on the new leader and record whether it commits.

latest_interpretation.rationale: Admission: a follower proposed the removal of the sitting leader (index 41). Results: the removed leader left leadership rather than continuing to lead a configuration it is no longer part of, reported as StateFollower with voter false and no leader (index 42, stepped_down true); with the clock advanced in rounds, node 2 reported StateLeader while the other two reported StateFollower, so a new leader was elected among the remaining voters (index 43, new_leader 2, not equal to zero); and a proposal made on that leader returned with no error and was committed, observed on nodes 2 and 3 but not on the removed node 1 (index 45), which matches the new configuration. All three comparisons are complete and satisfied. No defect is claimed; the transition behaved as the option documents, and it complements the other scenarios in which the option is off and a removed leader keeps leading. The observation also confirms the boundary of the parent investigation's harm: the removed node remains a follower that applies nothing new, which is different from the re-admitted member case.

knowledge.assertion: the removed leader stepped down, a remaining voter was elected, and the group committed afterwards

counterevidence: The election needed the clock to be advanced because elections are tick driven; the observation depends on the harness supplying clock progress.

Only one removal direction was executed (a follower removing the leader); a leader proposing its own removal while a leadership transfer is in progress was not exercised, which the source notes is a different path.
Reliable delivery and no partitions, so nothing about a removed leader that cannot hear the new configuration is claimed.
limitations: One scenario instance with three nodes and a single removal; no claim about repeated removals or larger groups.

The payload's presence on nodes 2 and 3 only is consistent with the new configuration, but the run does not assert anything about the removed node's future participation beyond its state and membership at the recorded indices.
No defect judgment: the documented transition held in this scenario.

knowledge.statement: node.run() keeps a local proposal gate armed only as a side effect of observing a leader change: when r.lead changes and a leader exists it sets propc = n.propc, when no leader exists it sets propc = nil, and after applying a conf change that removes the local node from the configuration it sets propc = nil. Applying a conf change that adds the local node back does not change the gate (the removal branch is guarded by okBefore && !okAfter, which is false for a re-addition), so the gate stays nil until the next observed leader change.
knowledge.conditions: Async Node API (node.run loop) with a single goroutine consuming Ready and calling ApplyConfChange for every conf change entry in Ready.CommittedEntries; the local node is a voter that sees a leader, is removed by a committed conf change, and is then re-added by a later committed conf change, with the same leader in place throughout.

knowledge.statement: node.Propose and node.ProposeConfChange hand a MsgProp to the run loop through stepWithWaitOption, which sends the request on the node's proposal channel n.propc (an unbuffered channel field that is always non-nil) and, when the call waits for a result, blocks until the run loop accepts the request or the caller's context or the node stop ends the wait. The run loop only receives from that channel while its own local gate variable is armed (set when an observed leader exists, cleared when the local member is removed and when no leader is observed), so while the gate is disarmed the caller's send is pending: it returns context.Canceled/DeadlineExceeded or ErrStopped only via those two exits, and it is admitted unmodified as soon as the gate is re-armed by an observed leader change.
knowledge.conditions: Async Node API run loop (node.go) with the local proposal gate disarmed, e.g. after the local member was removed by a committed conf change and before any observed leader change; caller either supplies a deadline or a context that never expires.

last_correction.correction: Previously recorded as 'when that channel is nil the send case cannot be selected'. The channel is not nil: the caller sends on n.propc (node.go:525) and blocks because the run loop's local gate variable is nil, so the receive case at node.go:386 cannot proceed until the gate is armed. Consequence for the claim: the pending invocation is admitted when the gate is re-armed (an observed leader change), so the non-completion window is bounded by the absence of an observed leader change rather than by the caller's context alone.

knowledge.statement: The raft state machine itself does not block a proposal from a member that is no longer in its own configuration: stepLeader returns ErrProposalDropped when the leader has no progress entry for itself (a removed leader), so the blocking behavior of a re-added voter is produced by the node wrapper's gate rather than by the state machine's proposal rules.
knowledge.conditions: State-leader step function with r.trk.Progress[r.id] == nil (local node removed from the active configuration).

knowledge.statement: The captured node-level test defines the intended proposal-blocking condition as 'does not know who is the current leader': it asserts that a Propose invocation on a node without a leader does not return, and then asserts that after the node campaigns and installs a leader the same pending invocation returns NoError. The test therefore scopes intended blocking to the unknown-leader case and expects acceptance once a leader is known; it exercises no removal/re-addition path and does not cover a member that is re-added while a leader is known.
knowledge.conditions: Single-voter test node driven through the async Node API (newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1)), newNode + go n.run()); the assertion is on the invocation issued before any leader is known, and on the same invocation once the node becomes leader.

knowledge.statement: In the retained three-node scenario, invocations on the re-added voter never completed and never delivered while other members' proposals were committed in the same intervals: invocation 1 (2500 ms context) had not returned after 1200 ms and released only with 'context deadline exceeded' at 2501 ms with no node holding its payload; retries 2 and 3 (900 ms contexts, 800 ms windows) also had not returned and their payloads were absent, and in each retry interval a proposal by never-removed node 2 returned in 0 ms and was committed on all three nodes. After the leader changed from 1 to 2 at term 2, the same invocation on the re-added voter returned in 0 ms and was committed on all three nodes.
knowledge.conditions: Async Node API, three nodes (1,2,3) in one process, reliable per-sender delivery, no ticks delivered; node 3 removed and re-added by committed conf changes with leader 1 unchanged throughout the non-completing invocations; each retry uses an independent context and operation id.

knowledge.statement: While the run loop's proposal gate is disarmed for the re-added voter, a configuration change proposed through Node.ProposeConfChange is held pending in the same way as an ordinary proposal: the invocation had not returned after 800 ms (it released only at its own 900 ms deadline, with an empty error at that point) and no node applied a conf change adding the proposed node. The gate therefore covers the administrative entry point of the same member, not only ordinary proposals.
knowledge.conditions: Async Node API, three nodes (1,2,3) in one process, reliable per-sender delivery, no ticks; node 3 removed and re-added by committed conf changes with leader 1 unchanged; the proposed change is ConfChange add node 9, a node that is not part of the cluster.

knowledge.statement: The same held-proposal effect is reached when the member's removal is expressed through joint consensus with automatic leave rather than as a simple configuration change. With a ConfChangeV2 whose transition is JointImplicit carrying remove node 3, node 3 applied one conf-change entry carrying the removal and was then excluded from both halves of its own configuration (voter false, outgoing false), and after it was re-added by a later committed change with leader 1 still unchanged, an ordinary invocation did not return inside a 1200 ms window, a configuration-change proposal did not return inside 800 ms, and an invocation with a context that never expires stayed pending through a 2000 ms window, while a never-removed member's invocation returned immediately and committed and, after a forced leader change, an invocation on node 3 returned immediately.
knowledge.conditions: Async Node API, three nodes (1,2,3) in one process, reliable per-sender delivery, no ticks; the removal is a ConfChangeV2 with Transition JointImplicit and a single remove change, so raft itself proposes the entry that leaves the joint state; the re-addition is a simple ConfChange.

knowledge.statement: Advancing the logical clock does not release a proposal held by the disarmed gate. In the retained run, ten rounds of Tick to every node (with message delivery between rounds, so leader heartbeats kept flowing and no election was triggered) left node 1 in StateLeader at term 1, the re-added node 3 a voter seeing leader 1, and the context-free invocation still pending; that invocation was admitted only after a forced campaign installed node 2 as leader at term 2, 4637 ms after it was issued, and its payload was committed on all three nodes.
knowledge.conditions: Async Node API, three nodes (1,2,3) in one process with ElectionTick 10 and HeartbeatTick 1; node 3 removed by joint-implicit configuration change and re-added by a committed change with leader 1 unchanged; ticks delivered in ten rounds with delivery between rounds; no message loss.

knowledge.statement: In the explored scope, no safety monitor reported a violation. Both seeds ran 300 driver steps over three real raft state machines with lossy, reordering-prone delivery and changing connectivity masks: seed 11 recorded 93 proposals, 9 campaigns, 12 leader-transfer requests, 434 messages delivered, 286 dropped and 19 distinct applied indexes; seed 23 recorded 95 proposals, 10 campaigns, 8 transfers, 303 delivered, 280 dropped and 10 distinct applied indexes. The event stream from that run contains no safety_violation event, so one leader per term, immutability of applied entries per node and index, cross-node agreement for an index, per-node commit monotonicity, and presence of previously applied entries in the log of a reporting leader were all unchecked-false in that scope.
knowledge.conditions: Exploratory basis without a fixed requirement: three state machines (ids 1,2,3, ElectionTick 10, HeartbeatTick 1) with in-memory storage whose ConfState is {1,2,3}; 300 steps per seed; per-node connectivity masks redrawn at random, per-message drop decisions, random ticks, random member proposals, random campaigns and random transfer requests; committed entries applied through the captured log interface with monitors checked after every step; membership changes deliberately not injected.

knowledge.statement: With membership changes injected, the explored scope again produced no safety violation. Seed 11 accepted 8 of 27 attempted conf-change proposals, ran 103 proposals, 15 campaigns, 15 leader-transfer requests, 204 messages delivered, 178 dropped, 16 distinct applied indexes, and reported zero violations; seed 23 accepted 2 of 18 attempts, ran 91 proposals, 4 campaigns, 8 transfers, 257 delivered, 177 dropped, 14 applied indexes, and reported zero violations. Neither run emitted a conf_change_apply_panic, a conf_change_unmarshal or a safety_violation event, so one leader per term, per-node immutability of applied entries, cross-node agreement for an index, per-node commit monotonicity and completeness at each leadership transition held in that scope.
knowledge.conditions: Exploratory basis without a fixed requirement: three state machines (ids 1,2,3, ElectionTick 10, HeartbeatTick 1) with in-memory storage whose ConfState is {1,2,3}; 300 steps per seed; per-node connectivity masks redrawn at random, per-message drop decisions, random ticks, random member proposals, random campaigns, random transfer requests and random membership-change proposals from a leader (add or remove learner ids 10 or 11, or remove or re-add voter 3); conf changes applied on application with apply panics recorded as events; completeness evaluated only at leadership transitions.

knowledge.statement: A member restarted from persisted state in the retained three-node scenario recovered the committed entry it had missed and returned to full participation. Before the restart the node's committed and applied index were both 2; after the restart it reported leader 1, applied the entry committed while it was down (committed and applied index 3), the payload appeared in its applied entries and on all three nodes (observed_nodes [3,1,2]), and a subsequent proposal from it returned with no error and its payload was committed on all three nodes.
knowledge.conditions: Async Node API, three nodes (1,2,3) in one process, no message loss and no snapshots; node 2 stopped while a payload was committed by nodes 1 and 3, then rebuilt on the same MemoryStorage that the driver had updated with HardState and appended entries; ten rounds of ticks with delivery between rounds after the restart so the leader issued heartbeats; membership unchanged.

knowledge.statement: The held-proposal effect persists under the recommended production configuration with a running clock. With Config.PreVote and Config.CheckQuorum enabled and ten rounds of ticks delivered with delivery between rounds, the leader remained node 1 in StateLeader at term 1 and the re-added node was a voter (index 38 of the receipt); its invocation had not returned after 900 ms inside a 1200 ms context (index 40) and its payload was committed nowhere (index 41), while the never-removed member's invocation returned with no error (index 43) and its payload was committed on all three nodes (index 44).
knowledge.conditions: Async Node API, three nodes (1,2,3) in one process with PreVote and CheckQuorum true, ElectionTick 10 and HeartbeatTick 1; node 3 removed by a committed simple ConfChange and re-added by a committed simple ConfChange with leader 1 unchanged; ticks delivered in ten rounds with delivery between rounds before the invocation; reliable delivery.

knowledge.statement: The proposal gate covers the MsgProp entry points of the Node API and nothing else. node.Propose, node.ProposeConfChange and node.Step with a MsgProp all end in stepWithWaitOption, which sends on n.propc, the channel the run loop only receives from while its gate variable is armed; every other message type, including MsgReadIndex, is sent on n.recvc instead. A member whose gate is disarmed therefore has its proposals and configuration proposals held, while its other duties - forwarding read-index requests to the leader it knows, answering messages and participating in replication and application - are not routed through the gate.
knowledge.conditions: Async Node API run loop in this snapshot, whichever configuration flags are used, with the run loop's gate variable disarmed for the local member; the boundary is now backed by a retained read-index control on a re-added member (read state observed, proposal held), in addition to the source anchors.

last_correction.correction: The earlier conditions said the statement was source-derived and had not been executed as a control. A read-index control was executed afterwards and is now cited, so the conditions no longer claim the boundary is unobserved. latest_interpretation.rationale: Ten retained executions establish the account. Witness: with node 3 dropped from both halves and re-admitted, and no leader change observed, invocations on it do not return inside the observed windows (1201 ms, 800/801 ms, 900 ms, 2000 ms), release only at the caller's deadline, leave no committed payload, and are admitted unmodified once a leader change re-arms the gate (4637 ms after issue) with
counterevidence: node.go:407-411 acknowledges the gate as improvised (propc is reset when the leader changes ... This isn't very sound and likely has bugs); this explains the dependence on leader changes but is neither a calling restriction nor a protection, and no other re-arm path exists in the snapshot.

node_test.go:352-385 shows that not returning is intended for a node that does not know the current leader. That expectation does not cover the witnessed case, and the same test expects acceptance once a leader is known.
No request is lost: held invocations are admitted unmodified once the gate is re-armed, so the harm is an unbounded wait without an error signal rather than data loss or a protocol safety violation.
limitations: Comparison outcomes for the earliest receipt were unknown because that harness gave the three operations' result events the same names; its decisive events are complete and match the successor receipts, which have complete holds.

Scope is the async Node API path (node.run loop) in this snapshot; RawNode.Propose and RawNode.ProposeConfChange have no such gate. Delivery is reliable throughout, so loss and partition behaviour is not characterized.

Clock schedules executed were ten rounds with delivery between rounds, under default flags and under PreVote plus CheckQuorum; partitions in which the member hears no leader traffic were not executed.

questions.question: With StepDownOnRemoval enabled, does a leader removed by a committed configuration change step down, do the remaining voters elect a new leader, and does the group keep reaching decisions?
questions.hypothesis: switchToConfig steps the removed leader down when the option is enabled, after which it is not promotable and the remaining voters campaign and elect one of themselves, so progress continues with the new configuration.
questions.discriminator: In the three-node Node-API cluster with StepDownOnRemoval true: elect node 1, have node 2 propose the removal of node 1, record node 1's state and membership after the change is applied, advance the clock until a leader other than node 1 emerges among the remaining voters, then propose a payload on the new leader and record whether it commits.

latest_interpretation.rationale: Admission: a follower proposed the removal of the sitting leader (index 41). Results: the removed leader left leadership rather than continuing to lead a configuration it is no longer part of, reported as StateFollower with voter false and no leader (index 42, stepped_down true); with the clock advanced in rounds, node 2 reported StateLeader while the other two reported StateFollower, so a new lea
counterevidence: The election needed the clock to be advanced because elections are tick driven; the observation depends on the harness supplying clock progress.

Only one removal direction was executed (a follower removing the leader); a leader proposing its own removal while a leadership transfer is in progress was not exercised, which the source notes is a different path.
Reliable delivery and no partitions, so nothing about a removed leader that cannot hear the new configuration is claimed.
limitations: One scenario instance with three nodes and a single removal; no claim about repeated removals or larger groups.

The payload's presence on nodes 2 and 3 only is consistent with the new configuration, but the run does not assert anything about the removed node's future participation beyond its state and membership at the recorded indices.
No defect judgment: the documented transition held in this scenario.

questions.hypothesis: The restarted instance reloads Term, Vote and Commit from its storage, learns the current leader from the leader's heartbeats, fetches the entries committed while it was down through the ordinary append path, applies them, and re-arms its proposal gate when it observes the leader, so it returns to full participation.

latest_interpretation.rationale: Both resynchronization paths are now retained and both satisfy their obligations. Append-path branch: the restarted member reported leader 1 and applied the entry committed while it was down (indices 37: commit and applied index 3, payload on all three nodes), then proposed successfully (indices 38, 39). Snapshot branch: the leader snapshotted at index 3 (term 1) and compacted to 3 (index 41), the
counterevidence: The clock was advanced by the harness in both branches; without ticks the restarted member receives no leader traffic in this setup, so the observations depend on the harness supplying clock progress rather than on the target alone.
The snapshot carries no application state machine data, so what is established is raft-level resynchronization (installation and subsequent participation), not state-machine content correctness.
Neither branch exercises storage loss, multiple restarts or crash-stop during snapshot installation.
limitations: Single restart per branch, one stopped member, reliable delivery and no ticks during the outage; no simultaneous restarts.
The snapshot branch compacts to the leader's last index in one step; incremental compaction interleaved with ongoing replication was not exercised.
One scenario instance per branch; the results establish observed behaviour rather than a general guarantee, and membership is unchanged so the storage's ConfState stays valid across the restart.

latest_interpretation.rationale: The exploration result stands as previously interpreted: both seeds completed 300 steps with zero reported safety violations, no conf-change apply panic and no unmarshal failure, across configurations that actually changed (8 and 2 accepted membership changes). The deterministic finding from the other investigation was reproduced inside the same execution before the exploration ran, so this negative is not a statement that the snapshot behaves correctly everywhere.
Election timings come from crypto/rand through the captured randomized election timeout, so interleavings differ between runs; the counters describe the retained run only.
limitations: Bounded scope: two seeds, 300 steps each, three nodes; snapshots, restart recovery inside the randomized run and crash-stop faults are excluded, and no absence or occurrence-rate claim is made.

The configuration axis is sampled thinly: only 8 and 2 membership changes were accepted, and the injected forms are limited to learner add/remove and removal or re-addition of voter 3.
